findings.title: Date override check skips busy-time validation
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot is not rejected by the override loop, the function returns true immediately before executing the busy.every check. This means existing bookings or calendar busy times are ignored for slots covered by a date override, which can expose already-booked slots and allow double bookings.

findings.title: Multiple date overrides for the same day are handled incorrectly
findings.body: The dateOverrides.find callback returns true when the slot is outside the particular override it is checking. If a user has multiple date overrides on the same date, a slot that is inside one override will be outside another override, causing find to return that other override and checkIfIsAvailable to return false. Valid slots can therefore be hidden whenever multiple date overrides exist for one day.

findings.title: Dayjs objects are compared with ===
findings.body: The condition `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two Dayjs object references, not their timestamps. This is never true for equal times. If a zero-length date override is used to represent an unavailable period or special case, this branch will not behave as intended. Use `.isSame()` instead.

findings.title: Date override date comparison depends on server local timezone
findings.body: The code formats `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` using the server's local timezone, while `slotStartTime` is formatted as UTC. If the server timezone is not UTC, a converted date override near midnight can be assigned to the wrong calendar date, causing overrides to be matched or ignored incorrectly. The comparison should use UTC explicitly.

findings.title: Working-hours validation rejects multi-interval schedules and can treat users with no hours as available
findings.body: The workingHours.find logic returns true when the slot is outside a particular working-hours interval. If a user has multiple working intervals in one day, a slot inside one interval is outside another interval, so the slot is rejected. Conversely, if the user has no working-hours entry for that weekday, the function falls through to the busy check and may mark the user available even though they have no availability. The check should require the slot to be contained in at least one working-hours interval and reject when none matches.

findings.title: Working-hours end time uses slot start instead of slot end
findings.body: In the working-hours check, `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` twice instead of using the slot end time or start time plus event length. As a result, a slot that starts before the working-hours end but extends past it passes the check, allowing bookings that run outside the configured availability.

findings.title: Active date override filter compares wall-clock override start as a UTC instant
findings.body: The override conversion treats `override.start` as a wall-clock time encoded in UTC, but activeOverrides filters by comparing `dayjs.utc(override.start)` directly against the invitee day's UTC interval. For large timezone offsets, this can exclude an override that belongs to the invitee date or include one that belongs to another date. For example, an override stored as 14:00Z for an invitee in UTC+14 may be filtered out because the invitee date spans roughly D-1 10:00Z to D 10:00Z, even though the converted local time is D 22:30.

findings.title: Timezone shift drops date changes when an override crosses midnight
findings.body: After adding the timezone offset, the code extracts only `.hour()` and `.minute()` to build startTime and endTime. If the offset moves the override across midnight, the date change is discarded. The override can then be placed on the wrong invitee day or produce an end time earlier than the start time, causing missing or incorrect slots.

findings.title: No regression test for round-robin fixed-host date overrides
findings.body: The PR description says it fixes date overrides for fixed hosts in round-robin events, but the added test only checks timezone conversion for a personal event. There is no automated test creating a round-robin event with a fixed host and asserting that only slots within the fixed host's date override are returned.
